newsitem.title: USA: US FCC to review foreign rules after telecom pact.
newsitem.headline: US FCC to review foreign rules after telecom pact.

text.p: U.S. regulators will review rules covering the entry of foreign phone companies into the United States and other proposed international regulations in response to the new global telecommunications pact, officials said Wednesday.

The Federal Communications Commission is conducting the review and will make changes to ensure its regulations conform with international trade law and the new global telecom accord aimed at opening up communications markets around the world.

Aside from the foreign-carrier entry rule, the agency plans to review proposed rules designed to slash the cost of foreign calls made from this country as well as the second proposed Domestic/International Satellite Consolidation order, or Disco 2.

The FCC adopted its foreign-carrier entry rule in November of 1995. The agency said it would block overseas investments in the U.S. telecommunications industry if a foreign company's home market curbs access to American communications firms.
FCC Chairman Reed Hundt and other officials told a news conference Wednesday the agency -- after its review -- would focus on whether such transactions would be in the "public interest."
That would allow the FCC to "scrutinize" whether a foreign acquisition or investment in "anyway distorts competition here in the United States," said Hundt.
"We made it very clear in the (WTO negotiations) that that was not going away. That that would still give us a lot of muscle."
Currently, the FCC focuses on whether the foreign carrier's home market is open to U.S. companies.
Hundt also said the FCC would "guarantee" the order is consistent with international trade rules governing "Most Favored Nation" status.
"We will be making a record on this topic," Hundt added. "We will be taking comments."
